title: Decon Latency Spectrometer: model-route IO-mode breakdown (p50/p95/p99)
creator: Marcus Li
description: Build a new dashboard and associated telemetry that decomposes end-to-end latency by model and route with an explicit IO-mode dimension (streaming vs non-streaming). The goal is to make it easy for SRE/Eng/PMs to surface regressions and understand whether slowdowns are due to streaming-related overhead (stream fanout/flushes) or blocking path components (scheduler, kernel, network). This ticket covers schema changes, aggregation queries, trace linking, dashboard panels, and alert definitions.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for every active (model,route) pair broken down by IO mode: streaming and non-streaming
Panels include: cohort histogram (latency buckets), delta waterfall (component attribution), and trace-link column that opens Jaeger/Tempo with trace_id prefilled
Metric/label schema includes io_mode label (values: streaming|blocking), request_shape label (short|medium|long), and model_version label
Queries perform within dashboard SLA (<2s for 24h window on staging ClickHouse), and cardinality is bounded via sensible rollup (route normalization + model tagging)
Automated alerts for p99 increase >25% sustained for 5m per route+model+io_mode and enrichment in incident payload with top-5 offending traces
Docs and runbook updated with how to interpret panels and next steps for triage
implementation_plan: 1) Telemetry schema: add 'io_mode' and 'request_shape' labels to latency histograms and summary metrics from the serving runtime (runtime team to instrument)
2) Metrics pipeline: update Kafka topic schema and ClickHouse materialized views to ingest new labels and maintain low-cardinality rollups per hour
3) Tracing: ensure trace_id is attached to every latency event and add trace_link generation helper in dashboard (tempo/jaeger URL template)
4) Queries: prototype ClickHouse aggregation for p50/p95/p99 and histogram buckets; add retention-friendly rollups for 7/30/90d
5) Dashboard: assemble panels in Console observability space — overview, per-route matrix, cohort histogram, waterfall decomposition, and trace table
6) Alerts & Runbook: create alert rules in Alertmanager and a playbook that attaches relevant dashboard and top traces to PagerDuty incidents
7) Testing & rollout: validate on staging with synthetic workloads (streaming-heavy and sync-heavy), run canary on 10% traffic, then full rollout
telemetry: Metric names: redwood.serve.latency_ms.histogram, redwood.serve.latency_ms.summary, redwood.serve.requests.count, redwood.serve.errors.count
Required labels: model, model_version, route, route_normalized, io_mode (streaming|blocking), request_shape (short|medium|long), region, deployment_tier
Trace enrichment: trace_id label on every request metric and an event-level 'first_chunk_time_ms' for streaming to compute stream startup latency
queries: ClickHouse example - p95: SELECT model, route_normalized, io_mode, quantileExact(0.95)(latency_ms) AS p95 FROM redwood_latency_mv WHERE event_time >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR GROUP BY model, route_normalized, io_mode

ClickHouse histogram buckets: SELECT model, route_normalized, io_mode, histogramBuild(toUInt64(latency_ms), [0,5,10,20,50,100,250,500,1000]) FROM redwood_latency WHERE event_time >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR GROUP BY model, route_normalized, io_mode
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2368 - spectrometer dashboard and trace linking helper
runbook: If p99 spikes for a model+route+io_mode: 1) open dashboard, 2) inspect cohort histogram and waterfall, 3) click trace link for top traces, 4) check recent deploys and kernel selection logs
Escalation: if error rate concurrently increases >2x, page on-call backend team and mark incident as customer-impacting
